5:T4ba,<p>Cache storages are used to reduce read and writes to disk by storing memory in RAM</p>
<p>Use cases:</p>
<ul>
<li>low latency</li>
<li>Improve disk (or DB) performance</li>
</ul>
<p>Suitable for data that is:</p>
<ul>
<li>Frequently accessed</li>
<li>Short lived</li>
<li>(Network cache) Needs to be shared throughout multiple distributed instances</li>
<li></li>
</ul>
<h1 id="redis">Redis</h1>
<p>A redis cache cluster is an in memory cache cluster that the application can make network calls to access. It is in memory since the data is stored in RAM on the cluster.</p>
<h1 id="off-heap-memory">Off Heap Memory</h1>
<p>Off heap cache is memory stored in RAM to be used as a cache directly on the application instance.</p>
<p>Pros:</p>
<ul>
<li>Faster</li>
<li>More secure and private</li>
<li>Easier to maintain
Cons:</li>
<li>Can't be used from multiple distributed instances without distributed locks</li>
</ul>
<p>Articles:</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://blogs.oracle.com/javamagazine/post/creating-a-java-off-heap-in-memory-database" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Creating a Java off-heap in-memory database</a>
<ul>
<li>Store data in RAM without garbage collection</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>b:X
